searches.reason: Develop paired probes that test whether BERT4Rec uses recent, specific context. On training-history prefixes, compare recent-item deletion with count-matched random deletion and latest-item-preserving shuffling, holding targets and candidates fixed. Measure target-rank changes and top-10 overlap with user-clustered uncertainty. Identity controls and deliberately corrupted MASK/readout controls should establish probe reliability; sensitivity alone does not establish user intent.

searches.reason: Connect the prespecified 0.75 terminal / 0.25 reconstruction objective to actual network behavior. Research inexpensive, read-only probes of branch-gradient norms, conflict and variance separately for embeddings and encoder layers, using exact loss denominators. Persist checkpoint-linked provenance and flag contradictions between measured allocation and metric definitions. This could distinguish objective interference from noisy sampling without training auxiliary models or changing the intervention.

searches.reason: Build a feedback-grounded audit distinguishing choose-now relevance, unnecessary duplication, explicit incompatibility and unidentified content. Use structured feedback from the twenty training users, supported only by supplied histories, titles and descriptions; missing compatibility evidence must remain unknown. Research annotation agreement, abstention and exposure denominators so rejection rates are trustworthy. Lexical similarity can identify cases for review but cannot establish ownership, fulfilled demand or incompatibility.
